questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My decision to study at UCSD was driven by three key factors: the desire for an authentic American collegiate experience, a long-standing interest in California’s culture, and the university’s reputation for academic excellence. Specifically, San Diego’s consistent climate offered a welcome contrast to the Danish winter, providing an ideal environment for both study and personal growth.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing once in a lifetime opertunity and experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, check your UCSD email frequently for information on events during welcome week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: To be honest, I didn't get much formal assistance from the uni when I first landed, but I found my feet through the off-campus housing portal. That’s actually where I met most of my international friends! Since I didn't know any others going from Denmark. I leaned on that international group early on. We ended up going to university events together, like the International Coffee Hour, which was a total game-changer for meeting even more people. My advice? Don't wait for a formal welcome—just start connecting with other internationals during the housing search.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard to find cheap housing as an exchange student who is there for only 6 months, but you can try you chances at the off campus housing portal. I chose Anatolia Housing, which is also recommended by the campus, and they offer shorter term leases with good amenities and give a chance of making new friends as you have a roommate and share the apartment with two additional flatmates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great, and I'm glad that I didnt get into Ihouse because parties at Ihouse are nonexistent, and the times we tried, it got shut down at 10 pm by the campus security. However, make sure that you dont live too far off campus. Living at Anatolia hosuing, Campus is 15 mins away by bus and public transport is also free for UCSD students through the pronto App.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: be prepared for some of the world’s most expensive housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you get into one of the UC's you get access to their website where you can enrool in cources make sure you do that on time if there are some specific courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student service have events to help you socialize and adapt to the culture and campus one week before the beginning of the quarter.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: People eventually drop out of courses during the first two weeks and you might be able to get the course even though you are waitlisted

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't like how much attendance and engagement affected the grades; it was the only thing stopping me from getting a 4.0 GPA

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is easier than UCPH, enjoy your time there without any academic pressure. I put in 30-40% of the effort I normally put in at UCPH and managed to get a 3.85 GPA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses have fewer students, and professors expect you to engage during lectures. Additionally, I had to do a presentation in 4/8 of my courses, which is unusual compared to ECON at UCPH, but don't fear, they are relatively gracious with the presentation grading.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was there for 2 quarters
1 Q: Game theory (p), Labor Economics, Business Finance (from the MGT major) and public policy
2 Q: Machine learning in business and econ, Leadership and organization (MGT 162), Industrial organization (p) and Economics of development (p)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make sure you enrool in minimum 3 priority courses, which UCPH requires

questions.answer: No unexpected costs other than traveling a lot. Be prepared to embark on travels and book your rentals like cars and housing in advance to save some money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beers are much more expensive compared to DK, but other groceries are about the same price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The uni has clubs for any activity that you might be interested in, and they will do tableing during the first week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the beach, go to all the national parks (grand canyon and Zion were one of my faves), go to vegas 5-6 hrs drive and party a lot in PB go to Hideaway on thursdays and Moonshine on Fridays and saturdays.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on the Hike close to campus, like the "Ho chi min trial"
La Jolla Shores Beach is the prettiest but there are other beaches close to campus that are nice to visit.
Go taco hunting- SD has some of the best mexican food places (Get the cali burito (most value for money))

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Put yourself out there and every new international is on the same boat seeking new friendships

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly locals at la jolla and the laid back vibe of California

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get the insurance through ISO (international student health insurance) instead of UC-ship, and waive the UC-ship, this will save you around 3000 dkk.
Get housing at costa verde (anatolia housing) if you don't get a spot a Ihouse, as the spots are limited, here you will meet other internationals.
Get a car with your flatmates or by yourself for convenience, but keep in mind that parking spots on campus are limited and relatively expensive pr hour.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get memberships at the stores like vons or ralphs to save on gorceries
Make sure you know which courses are offered in each quarter, as all the courses listed on the websites are not offered each quarter

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to build new relationships across nations and getting to travel and experience a new culture with these amazing people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Although I didn't face many challenges, I did get a bit homesick early on. Once I adapted, it became one of the best experiences of my life

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
